chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan, who said:

I prayed behind Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام for several days, and he would recite in Fatihat al-Kitab: Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Then when it was a prayer in which the recitation is not done aloud, he would recite Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim aloud, and keep the rest lower.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu 'Abd Allah, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام
key_terms.بِبِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ: the basmalah formula recited at the beginning of the surah
key_terms.خَلْفَ: behind, following as an imam-led prayer
key_terms.فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: the Opening of the Book, the opening surah recited in salat
key_terms.وَأَخْفَى: he kept it quiet or subdued

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام recite Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim aloud in quiet prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the practice of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام in salat regarding the recitation of Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim in Fatihat al-Kitab. It indicates that even in prayers where recitation is normally not audible, he would pronounce the basmalah aloud while keeping the remainder quiet, highlighting its distinct liturgical status.
